bib.title: ROUGE: A Package for Automatic Evaluation of Summaries
bib.venue: ACL 2004 Workshop on Text Summarization Branches Out (as an ACL workshop paper; venue not printed in text)

question: How well do automatic n-gram, LCS, weighted LCS and skip-bigram overlap measures between candidate and reference summaries agree with human judgments of summary quality?
hypothesis: Following BLEU in machine translation, overlap statistics against human reference summaries should correlate with human coverage judgments.
contributions: Introduces the ROUGE package with ROUGE-N, ROUGE-L, ROUGE-W, ROUGE-S and ROUGE-SU
Evaluates 17 ROUGE measures against human judgments on DUC 2001, 2002, 2003 data with bootstrap confidence intervals
Shows normalized pairwise LCS in MEAD is an F-measure with beta=1 and sentence-level equals ROUGE-L

method.summary: Defines recall-oriented overlap measures and computes system-level correlation between mean ROUGE scores and mean human coverage scores over DUC 2001-2003 systems, across single/multiple references, case/stem/stopword settings.

datasets.name: DUC 2001/2002/2003 human judgments
datasets.size: Single-doc ~100 words: 12 systems (2001, 149 summaries judged/system), 14 systems (2002, 295/system); single-doc ~10 words: 14 systems (2003, 624/system); multi-doc: 10 words 6 systems (2002); 50 words 14 (2001) and 10 (2002); 100 words 14 (2001), 10 (2002), 18 (2003); 200 words 14 (2001), 10 (2002); 400 words 14 (2001). Multi-doc summaries judged per system: 29 (2001), 59 (2002), 30 (2003).
datasets.source: NIST DUC; each system set includes 1 or 2 baselines; manual summary sets: 3 (2001), 2 (2002), 4 (2003)

other.measures: ROUGE-N N=1..9, ROUGE-L, ROUGE-W alpha=1.2, ROUGE-S and ROUGE-SU with dskip=1(*),4,9 (tables label * for unlimited)

inference.samples: Jackknifing over M references: best score over M sets of M-1 references, averaged; max over references for multi-reference

parameters.beta_in_DUC: set to a very big number so only recall R_lcs counts (text prints 'β set to a very big number')
parameters.ROUGE-W weighting: f(k)=k^alpha, alpha=1.2 in package; k^2 in worked example
parameters.ROUGE-S max skip distance: d_skip = 1, 4, 9 tested; 0 equals bigram overlap F-measure
parameters.ROUGE-SU: adds unigram counting unit (equivalent to begin-of-sentence marker)

metrics.name: Pearson correlation of system-average ROUGE vs average human coverage
metrics.definition: Product moment correlation across systems; also Spearman and Kendall computed but only Pearson reported; 95% CI by bootstrap resampling

metrics.name: Human coverage score (SEE)
metrics.definition: Judges compare a manual summary unit (EDU or sentence) with the candidate; overall score is the average content coverage over units of the manual summary; judges used only one manual summary

eval.protocol: 18 data points per measure per task (2 single/multi x 3 CASE/STEM/STOP x 3 correlations); critical Pearson r at 95% is 0.632 with 8 df, 0.576 (10), 0.532 (12), 0.497 (14), 0.468 (16)

limits: Correlations are system-level over only 6-18 systems; multi-document tasks have about 30 samples per system, which the author says destabilises correlation estimates
Only Pearson reported; Spearman and Kendall said to track it closely but not shown
Human judges used one manual summary even when multiple were available
Multi-document correlations rarely reach high 90s; achieving them is stated an open problem
Surface overlap: ROUGE-L counts only one LCS (S4 ties S3), ROUGE-S gives zero for reversed sentence (S5)
Evaluated on extractive-era news summarisation systems of 2001-2003, not abstractive/LLM output (dated)
Recall-oriented: with beta very large only recall is used, so length is not penalised in the DUC setting (inferred from the beta setting)

terms.definition: n-gram recall between a candidate summary and a set of reference summaries
any pair of words in their sentence order, allowing for arbitrary gaps

lineage.note: ROUGE-N is the recall counterpart of precision-based BLEU

lineage.work: Lin and Hovy 2003, Automatic evaluation of summaries using n-gram co-occurrence statistics
lineage.note: Showed BLEU-like n-gram statistics can evaluate summaries
Content-based similarity (cosine, unit overlap, LCS) without human correlation

lineage.work: Radev et al. 2002 (MEAD normalized pairwise LCS)
lineage.note: Shown to be an F-measure with beta=1
Separate study of the same measures for machine translation
